I am 35 years old and have farmed my family's land in Quzhou since I finished junior high school. We have six mu of flat, good-quality land here on the North China Plain, and like my father and most of my neighbors, I follow the wheat-maize double-cropping system. My winter wheat went into the ground last October after rotary tilling and sowing with an improved variety I bought from the county supply store. I applied one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as a basal dose then.

Now it is early spring, and the wheat is waking up. This year I will topdress with urea when I do the first irrigation at green-up, then irrigate again at jointing and once more at grain filling—three times total from the well. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice; if the weather turns damp, I might add a fungicide spray. I expect about 980 kg per mu from this wheat if the weather cooperates.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. I always buy hybrid maize seed from the county shop—this year I am thinking of a variety like Nongda 372 or Denghai 605 because they yield well here. I will do rotary tillage before maize sowing to break up the stubble, then apply compound fertilizer as basal. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat, so I will water twice: once around tasseling and once during grain filling. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borer. I should get around 1,150 kg per mu from the maize. I stick to this rotation because the land and the market here are reliable for these two crops, and I know the inputs and timing by heart.
